pageDescription: The gluetun VPN that qui runs behind, the MyAnonamouse dynamic seedbox IP, your Sonarr, Radarr, Prowlarr, Bazarr and Tautulli apps, and your Jellyfin and Plex servers.

vpn.title: VPN
vpn.description: From gluetun's control server: the tunnel, the IP it exits from and the forwarded port.

restartDialog.title: Restart the gluetun container?
restartDialog.description: Docker restarts gluetun and waits until its health check passes. Torrents lose their connection until the VPN is back. Restart VPN is the lighter option when only the tunnel is stuck.
restartDialog.withDependents: Then restart the containers that share its network: {{containers}}
restartDialog.dependentsHelp: Without this, those containers keep a dead network until they restart. If qui is one of them, this page reloads when qui is back.

steps.waiting: Waiting for gluetun to report healthy…
steps.dependents: Restarting the containers that share its network…

dependents.title: Shared network
dependents.description: Containers that run with network_mode: "service:gluetun". Their traffic leaves through the VPN.
dependents.none: No other container uses gluetun's network.
dependents.name: Container

logs.title: Gluetun logs
logs.description: The container log from Docker. In view: {{errors}} errors, {{warnings}} warnings.

environment.title: Environment
environment.description: Variables the container sets on top of the image defaults, as in your compose file. Keys and passwords are hidden.
environment.unavailable: Docker access is needed to read the environment.
environment.empty: The container uses the image defaults only.
environment.name: Variable

vpnSettings.title: VPN settings
vpnSettings.description: The settings gluetun is running with, from its control server. Keys and passwords are hidden.

control.title: Control server
control.description: gluetun's HTTP control server gives the VPN status, the public IP and the forwarded port, and starts and stops the VPN.
control.urlHelp: With network_mode: "service:gluetun" qui shares gluetun's network, so http://127.0.0.1:8000 works.
control.authHelp: The control server needs authentication since gluetun v3.40. Set HTTP_CONTROL_SERVER_AUTH_DEFAULT_ROLE on gluetun, for example '{"auth":"apikey","apikey":"…"}'.
control.secretSaved: Saved, leave empty to keep it

docker.title: Docker
docker.description: Logs, health, resource use and container restarts come from the Docker API.
docker.enableHelp: Needs the Docker socket in the qui container. Anyone who can use the socket controls the host.
docker.hostHelp: unix:///var/run/docker.sock for a mounted socket, or tcp://host:2375 for a socket proxy. A container restart needs the socket: a TCP proxy is out of reach while gluetun restarts.
docker.composeHelp: Mount the socket and give qui the docker group. The entrypoint drops extra groups when PUID/PGID are set, so use user: instead:

outcomes.waiting: MAM sees {{ip}}. Add a mam_id to start updating.
outcomes.throttled: MAM says the last change was too recent. The next check retries.

toasts.removed: mam_id removed. Updates pause until you add one.

removeDialog.title: Remove the mam_id?
removeDialog.description: qui stops updating your seedbox IP on MyAnonamouse until you add a new mam_id.

status.title: Seedbox IP
status.description: What MyAnonamouse saw on the last check. Requests leave through gluetun, so this is the VPN's IP.
status.never: qui has not contacted MAM yet.
status.rejectedHelp: This session cannot be updated from this connection. Create a new dynamic seedbox session for the VPN, locked to its ASN, and paste the new mam_id.
status.unreachableHelp: This usually means the VPN is down. Check the Gluetun overview.

session.title: Session (mam_id)
session.description: The cookie of a MyAnonamouse session made for dynamic seedbox use. It is stored encrypted, and qui saves the new value when MAM rotates it.

steps.open: On MyAnonamouse, open <mam>Preferences → Security</mam> and create a session.
steps.ip: IP: the VPN's IP as MAM sees it ({{ip}}), not your browser's IP.
steps.asn: IP vs ASN locked session: ASN, so the IP can change within your VPN provider.
steps.dynamic: Allow Session to set Dynamic Seedbox: Yes. Use a separate session for qui.
steps.paste: Copy the cookie value MAM shows and paste it here.

session.label: mam_id

schedule.title: Schedule
schedule.description: MAM answers "No change" when the IP is the same, so frequent checks are harmless.
schedule.enabledHelp: Turn off to update only with Update now.
schedule.invalid: Enter a whole number of minutes between 1 and 1440.

activity.title: Activity
activity.description: Every request to MAM from the last 14 days, newest first (up to 50).

empty.description: Add your Sonarr, Radarr, Prowlarr, Bazarr and Tautulli servers to see their status, downloads, missing items, wanted subtitles, indexers and streams here.

manage.title: Apps
manage.description: Add as many instances of each app as you run, for example Sonarr and Sonarr 4K. qui only reads from them.

form.name: Name
form.urlHelp: The address qui uses to reach the app, including any URL base, for example http://192.168.1.10:8989/sonarr.
form.apiKeySaved: Saved, leave empty to keep it

keyHelp.sonarr: Find the API key in Sonarr under Settings → General → Security.
keyHelp.radarr: Find the API key in Radarr under Settings → General → Security.
keyHelp.prowlarr: Find the API key in Prowlarr under Settings → General → Security.
keyHelp.bazarr: Find the API key in Bazarr under Settings → General → Security.
keyHelp.tautulli: Find the API key in Tautulli under Settings → Web Interface → API. Turn on Enable API.

deleteDialog.title: Delete {{name}}?
deleteDialog.description: qui stops tracking this app. Nothing changes in the app itself.

help.title: Reaching your apps from qui
help.description: Each app can run inside gluetun or outside it; qui reaches it at the URL you enter. qui's own traffic leaves through gluetun, so apps outside it need a firewall exception.
help.sameNetwork: An app that also runs with network_mode: "service:gluetun" is at http://127.0.0.1 with its port.
help.lan: For an app on your LAN or another Docker network, add its network to FIREWALL_OUTBOUND_SUBNETS on gluetun, for example 192.168.1.0/24,172.16.0.0/12. Otherwise the gluetun firewall blocks the connection.
help.names: Use an IP address: gluetun's DNS cannot resolve Docker container names.
help.urlBase: If the app runs under a URL base, such as /sonarr behind a reverse proxy, include it in the URL.

library.noMatches: Nothing matches the search and filter.
library.partialTitle: Some instances could not be loaded

movies.title: Movies
movies.description: Every movie in your Radarr instances. Click a title to open it in Radarr.
movies.noInstances: Add a Radarr instance to see your movies here.

series.title: Series
series.description: Every series in your Sonarr instances. Episode counts include monitored episodes that have aired. Click a title to open it in Sonarr.
series.noInstances: Add a Sonarr instance to see your series here.

subtitles.title: Wanted subtitles
subtitles.description: Episodes and movies that Bazarr is still looking for subtitles for. Click a title to open it in Bazarr.
subtitles.noInstances: Add a Bazarr instance to see wanted subtitles here.

issues.title: Issues
issues.description: Everything that needs attention across your apps: apps that are down, health warnings, downloads that are stuck or failed, and failing indexers.
issues.none_one: No issues. Your app is healthy.
issues.none_few: No issues. All {{count}} apps are healthy.
issues.none_many: No issues. All {{count}} apps are healthy.
issues.none_other: No issues. All {{count}} apps are healthy.

empty.title: No media servers yet
empty.description: Add your Jellyfin and Plex servers to see their status here and to sync what each person watched between them.

summary.syncDescription: The last sync of each pair of servers.

servers.title: Media servers
servers.description: The Jellyfin and Plex servers qui reads status from and syncs watched state between.
servers.deleteDescription: qui stops tracking this server and deletes the sync pairs that use it, with their account maps and log. Nothing changes on the server itself.

help.title: Before you start
help.description: What qui needs from each server.
help.plexUsers: On Plex, qui syncs the owner and every account you share the server with. It asks plex.tv for each account's access, so qui needs internet access.
help.ids: Titles match on IMDb, TMDB and TVDB IDs. A title that has none of these on both servers cannot sync, so keep the metadata agents up to date.

form.urlHelp: The address qui uses to reach the server, for example http://192.168.1.10:8096 for Jellyfin or http://192.168.1.10:32400 for Plex.
form.tokenSaved: Saved, leave empty to keep it

tokenHelp.jellyfin: Jellyfin: create an API key under Dashboard → API Keys. An API key can read and mark watched items for every user.
tokenHelp.plex: Plex: use the X-Plex-Token of the server owner. Open any item in Plex Web, choose Get Info → View XML, and copy the X-Plex-Token value from the address.

pairs.none: No sync pairs yet. Add one to start syncing.
pairs.needServers: A sync pair links two media servers. Add at least two servers to set one up.
pairs.description: How watched state flows between {{a}} and {{b}}. qui only marks titles as watched; it never marks anything unwatched.
pairs.scheduleHelp: Off: sync only when you press Sync now on the Sync activity page.
pairs.invalidInterval: Enter a whole number of minutes between {{min}} and {{max}}.
pairs.deleteDescription: qui stops syncing these servers and deletes the account maps and the log of this pair. Watched state on the servers stays as it is.
pairs.addDescription: Pick two servers and the direction. You map the accounts next.

both.label: Both ways ({{a}} ⇄ {{b}})
both.description: A title watched on either server is marked watched on the other.

a_to_b.label: {{a}} to {{b}} only
a_to_b.description: {{a}} is the source. Titles watched on {{a}} are marked watched on {{b}}; {{a}} is never changed.

b_to_a.label: {{b}} to {{a}} only
b_to_a.description: {{b}} is the source. Titles watched on {{b}} are marked watched on {{a}}; {{b}} is never changed.

accounts.title: Accounts to sync
accounts.noPairs: Add a sync pair on the Sync direction page first.
accounts.description: Each row says that an account on {{a}} and an account on {{b}} are the same person. Only mapped accounts sync.
accounts.none: No accounts mapped yet. Use Match by name or Add row.
accounts.incomplete: Pick an account on both servers in every row, or remove the row.
accounts.usersFailed: Could not list the accounts on {{server}}: {{error}}

activity.title: Sync activity
activity.logDescription: The runs of the last 30 days, newest first.
activity.noMaps: Map at least one account on the Accounts page first.
activity.manualOnly: Syncs only when you press Sync now
activity.nothingMarked: This sync marked nothing: both servers already agreed.
activity.truncated_one: Only the first {{count}} title is listed.
activity.truncated_few: Only the first {{count}} titles are listed.
activity.truncated_many: Only the first {{count}} titles are listed.
activity.truncated_other: Only the first {{count}} titles are listed.

cancelDialog.title: Stop this sync?
cancelDialog.description: Titles already marked stay watched. The next sync picks up the rest.

prompt.sourceLibrary: Pick songs only from my music library, which is in the attached file: one artist per line, then one indented line per album, "Album: title | title".
prompt.sourceAny: Pick any songs that are on streaming services such as Spotify and YouTube Music.

create.title: Make a playlist with an AI assistant
create.description: Use ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or any other assistant. qui writes the prompt; you paste the answer back.
create.step1Description: Download your library as a text file and attach it to the chat, so the assistant picks songs you have. Skip this step for Spotify or YouTube Music playlists of any songs.
create.noServer: Add a Jellyfin or Plex server to export your library.
create.exported: Library downloaded ({{size}} KB). Attach the file to your chat.
create.step2Title: Describe the playlist and copy the prompt
create.step2Description: Write what you want to hear. Copy the prompt, paste it into the assistant, and attach the library file.
create.requestPlaceholder: Upbeat 2000s indie for a morning run, no ballads
create.step3Description: Paste the whole answer of the assistant. qui reads the JSON, or one "Artist - Title" per line.
create.name: Name (optional)

list.title: Playlists
list.description: Open a playlist to sync it to Jellyfin, Plex, Spotify or YouTube Music, or to compare it with a playlist there.
list.none: No playlists yet. Make one above.
list.name: Name
list.deleteDescription: qui forgets this playlist. The copies on Jellyfin, Plex, Spotify and YouTube Music stay.

detail.noServices: Not on any service yet. Add one to create the playlist there.
detail.removeDescription: qui stops syncing this playlist there. The playlist on the service stays.
detail.title: Title
detail.saveHint: Saving changes only qui. Press Sync to change the services too.

add.title: Add to a service
add.description: Copy {{name}} to Jellyfin, Plex, Spotify or YouTube Music.
add.newDescription: qui creates the playlist there with every track it finds.
add.existingLabel: Use a playlist that is already there
add.existingDescription: qui compares both and lets you choose what each side keeps.
add.noRemote: No playlists found on this account.

compare.title: Compare with {{service}}
compare.description: Tick what to keep. Applying writes your choice to both qui and "{{name}}" on {{service}}.

toasts.spotifyAppSaved: Spotify app saved. Now sign in.

setup.serversDescription: Playlists use the servers you added under Media servers → Servers. Nothing more to set up.
setup.serversAccount: You pick the account when you add a playlist to a server. On Plex, qui can write for the owner and every account you share the server with.
setup.serversMatch: A track syncs when that account's music library has it, matched by artist and title.
setup.spotifyDescription: qui signs in with your own Spotify app, so it needs a client ID and secret.

spotifySteps.dashboard: Open the <dashboard>Spotify developer dashboard</dashboard>, sign in, and click Create app. Any name and description will do.
spotifySteps.redirect: Under Redirect URIs, add the redirect URI shown in the field below, exactly as written:
spotifySteps.api: Under "Which API/SDKs are you planning to use?", tick Web API, then save.
spotifySteps.credentials: Open the app's Settings, copy the Client ID and the Client secret into the fields below, check the redirect URI, and click Save app.
spotifySteps.signIn: Click Sign in with Spotify and allow access.
spotifySteps.finish: With qui's own address, Spotify brings you back to this page and the sign-in is done. With the default 127.0.0.1 address, the browser shows an error page instead: that is expected. Copy the whole address from the address bar, paste it below, and click Connect. This works from any computer, wherever qui runs.

setup.spotifyPremium: Spotify only runs apps in Development Mode for accounts with Premium: the account that created the app needs Premium. Up to 5 accounts can use the app; add other accounts under User Management.
setup.ytDescription: YouTube Music has no public API, so qui signs in like your browser, with its cookie.
setup.ytWarning: This uses the private API of the YouTube Music website and may stop working when Google changes it. The cookie gives full access to your Google account: qui stores it encrypted. Signing out of YouTube in that browser also signs qui out; then paste new headers.

ytSteps.open: Open <ytm>music.youtube.com</ytm> in your browser and sign in.
ytSteps.devtools: Open the developer tools (F12) and go to the Network tab. Type browse in the filter box.
ytSteps.request: Click Library or Home in YouTube Music, so a POST request to browse shows in the list. Click it.
ytSteps.copy: Firefox: right-click the request and choose Copy Value → Copy Request Headers. Chrome or Edge: right-click it and choose Copy → Copy as cURL (bash).
ytSteps.paste: Paste everything below and click Connect.

setup.redirectHelp: It must match the app in the Spotify dashboard exactly. Spotify only accepts https:// addresses, or http://127.0.0.1. Use qui's address when you reach qui over HTTPS, for example behind a reverse proxy; otherwise keep the default.
setup.redirectNeedsHttps: You reach qui over http://, which Spotify does not accept here. Open qui through its HTTPS address first, or use the default.
